description: Canonical list of ALL Applied AI Network dashboard API integrations. Ground truth for the hub website template and for the Website tab in dashboard.all-ai-network.org, which generates the agent prompt from it. Every module is reachable WITHOUT an API key via the public bundle (see each module's publicSource) — that is the correct route for static sites and SPAs, which cannot hold a secret. The authenticated /api/v1/* endpoints are for sites that execute code on a server. Edit this file to add or change integrations.

integrations.title: Hub-site configuration
integrations.description: Fetch your chapter's theme colors, logo URL, and section toggles from the dashboard. Drives the site's CSS variables, header logo, and which components render.

snippets.agentPrompt:
Render this from the chapter's dashboard so the eboard controls it without touching this repo.

The chapter's dashboard-side presentation settings: theme colors, logo URL, display name/tagline, and per-section on/off toggles.

IMPORTANT — only apply these if this site was BUILT to be remotely themed. A site with its own established design should read the name, tagline and logo at most, and ignore theme colors and section toggles entirely. Overwriting a bespoke design with dashboard colors is the single most common way this integration goes wrong.

If you do apply the theme, set it as CSS custom properties on the root and let existing styles consume them — never duplicate the colors into individual rules. Missing section keys default to on.

Where it comes from: the public bundle's `config` field — GET /api/public/chapter/{slug}/bundle. No API key, CORS-open, safe to call from the browser. If this site runs code on a server at request or build time you may use the authenticated per-module endpoint above instead; if it does not (static site or SPA), use the bundle and do not introduce a key.

How to fit it in:
- If the site already has a section showing this, REWIRE it — change its data source and leave its markup and styling alone. Only build something new if nothing equivalent exists.
- Match the site's existing components, spacing, and type scale. Inspect a sibling section before writing any CSS.
- Escape remote text; only linkify http(s) URLs.
- Empty response → omit the section entirely rather than render an empty shell. Fetch failure → leave the page exactly as it was.

integrations.title: Upcoming events
integrations.description: Render your chapter's next events on your homepage. Auto-updates as you add events in the dashboard.

queryParams.name: upcoming
queryParams.description: Return only events in the future

queryParams.name: limit
queryParams.description: Max number of events to return (1-100)

snippets.agentPrompt:
Render this from the chapter's dashboard so the eboard controls it without touching this repo.

The chapter's events: title, description, type, start/end, timezone, location or virtual URL, cover image, attendance points, and phases for multi-part events. Co-hosted events include the host chapter so you can credit them.

Scope matters: the bundle returns ONLY UPCOMING events by default. A chapter whose events are all in the past gets an empty array — check the `events_scope` field before concluding it has none. Add `?events=all` for a full archive (newest first), `?events=past`, or `&events_limit=N` to raise the cap. A site with an events history page wants `all`; a homepage strip wants the default.

Show at least title, a human-formatted date in the event's own timezone, and location. Link to the event's own page if the site has one.

Where it comes from: the public bundle's `events` field — GET /api/public/chapter/{slug}/bundle. No API key, CORS-open, safe to call from the browser. If this site runs code on a server at request or build time you may use the authenticated per-module endpoint above instead; if it does not (static site or SPA), use the bundle and do not introduce a key.

How to fit it in:
- If the site already has a section showing this, REWIRE it — change its data source and leave its markup and styling alone. Only build something new if nothing equivalent exists.
- Match the site's existing components, spacing, and type scale. Inspect a sibling section before writing any CSS.

integrations.title: Projects & research
integrations.description: The chapter's project and research history — each with its team, papers, slides, and recordings.

snippets.agentPrompt:
Render this from the chapter's dashboard so the eboard controls it without touching this repo.

The chapter's project and research history. Each project has a title, description, cover image, school year, the team that built it (`members`, in byline order), and `files` — papers, slide decks, and recordings, each tagged with a `kind`.

The team and the papers are the point. A project list without names is a wall of titles; with names it's a record of who did what, and alumni will look themselves up. Show the byline and link any paper prominently.

Group by `year` if the chapter has several years of history — that's usually the most legible ordering. `files` may be empty; `members` may be a single name.

Where it comes from: the public bundle's `projects` field — GET /api/public/chapter/{slug}/bundle. No API key, CORS-open, safe to call from the browser. integrations.title: Learning tree
integrations.description: The network's shared AI curriculum graph merged with this chapter's own nodes.

publicSource.note: Its own endpoint — not part of the bundle.

snippets.agentPrompt:
Render this from the chapter's dashboard so the eboard controls it without touching this repo.

The curriculum graph: the network's shared base tree merged with the chapter's own nodes, as `nodes` + `edges`. Each node carries a title, summary, optional markdown body, tags, thumbnail, difficulty, prerequisites, and a `source` marking it as shared or chapter-authored.

Respect `pos_x`/`pos_y` where present — an officer arranged those by hand in the dashboard, and overriding them with an auto-layout throws away deliberate work. Only compute positions for nodes that have none.

`prereqs` can name more than one parent: this is a graph, not a strict tree, so a renderer that assumes one parent per node will silently drop edges.

If the site already renders a tree from its own data file, this endpoint replaces that file as the source of truth — the chapter edits nodes in the dashboard from now on.

Where it comes from: the public bundle's `nodes` field — GET /api/public/chapter/{slug}/bundle. No API key, CORS-open, safe to call from the browser. If this site runs code on a server at request or build time you may use the authenticated per-module endpoint above instead; if it does not (static site or SPA), use the bundle and do not introduce a key.
